rv.q: Blurs time and space in magically uplifting and soulful ways

The result is playful, elusive, sometimes frustrating and ultimately moving: a boldly experimental piece that meditates on home, on belonging and on the way both theatre and technology can seemingly bend time and shrink the space between people.
It is wonderful to get this glimpse into the future of theatre on the stage that once hosted the brave new worlds of John Osborne and Caryl Churchill.

This latest piece builds on Soleimanpour’s signature style, but the results are uneven – it is an inelegant collision of earnest philosophising intermingled with metatheatrical commentary on the distance between author, actor and audience.
These fragile moments shuffle closest to Soleimanpour's hopeful description of theatre as a time capsule, a way to hold on to people and the places we love even when we can't do so in person.
At its best ‘ECHO’ is moving, profound and visually stunning, but it comes saddled with a load of baggage from Soleimanpour being ‘the cold read guy’.
And while this particular show can be stimulating in its execution and heartening in its message of human togetherness it’s also, on a moment-by-moment level, rather boring.
This blend helps make his latest, ECHO (Every Cold-Hearted Oxygen), a uniquely enriching experience.
It’s beautiful, funny, confusing and penetrating in equal measure, and while this kind of high concept theatre often threatens to become gimmicky, Soleimanpour’s work still surprises every time.
ECHO certainly fulfils that admirable desire.
However, whilst I enjoyed the performance, I do not feel it will endure as a classic of either story-telling or theatre.
Ultimately, the most telling line ”We are all immigrants across time” defines what remains an extraordinary experience...

cn.t: Soleimanpour's experimental "cold read" format—featuring unrehearsed actors performing nightly—divides critics. Most find it an ingenious, moving meditation on exile and home, though some feel the gimmick overshadows uneven philosophical content.
